topics.label: Introduction to the lecture and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and establishes the learning objectives and scope for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities of cancer treatment, specifically surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their mechanisms and clinical limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and genetic defects in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeting oncogene addiction with kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the concept of oncogene addiction and the application of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, detailing their structural mechanisms, resistance pathways, and clinical management.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the design and therapeutic mechanisms of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates used to target cancer cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for immune surveillance and evaluate various immunotherapy strategies, including checkpoint blockade, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Contemporary challenges, future directions, and clinical dilemmas in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review overall progress and contemporary challenges in oncology, considering genomic stratification, prevention versus cure, and ethical considerations surrounding treatment options.
